newsitem.title: USA: Clinton picks Albright for secretary of state.
newsitem.headline: Clinton picks Albright for secretary of state.

text.p: President Bill Clinton decided on Thursday to name U.N. Ambassador Madeleine Albright as his next secretary of state, an administration official said.
The official, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the decision might be announced later on Thursday.
Albright was offered the job by Clinton in a telephone call Thursday, sources said. She would become the first woman to serve as U.S. secretary of state.

Her selection, which would require Senate confirmation, follows a protracted period of deliberation by Clinton seeking to form a national security team that can work together for his second four-term. He was re-elected on November 5.

Officials said Clinton's current national security adviser, Anthony Lake, would be nominated to take over as Central Intelligence Agency director and that Lake's deputy, Samuel Berger, would succeed Lake.
CNN said retiring Republican Senator William Cohen of Maine would be nominated to replace William Perry as defence secretary. He would be the first Republican in an otherwise Democratic Cabinet.
